person.persName: Lakṣmana or Lakṣṃīdhara (before saṃnyāsa, see notes)

person.note: He copied Kṛṣṇānanda Sarasvatī's Siddhāntasiddhāñjana in 1670.

He is different from another Rāmānanda Sarasvatī, the author of a subcommentary on Śaṅkara's Brahmasūtrabhāṣya called Ratnaprabhā and a treatise aligned with the Vivaraṇa interpretation of the Brahmasūtras titled Vivaraṇopanyāsa. See Duquette, Jonathan. Debates in the Delta: An Intellectual History of Late Advaita. Brill, forthcoming.
It is possible that he was called Rāmayati. See New Catalogus Catalogurum (NCC). Vols 1-36: vol. 24, p. 202b.

According to V. Krishnamacharya, Rāmānanda is the name undertaken by Lakṣmaṇa (or Lakṣmīdhara) of the Carakūri family. Before he became a saṃnyāsin with the name Rāmānanda, after being married for a long time, under the preceptor Kṛṣṇānandayati (author of the Siddhāntasiddhāñjana), he authored the following: 1) Ṣaḍbhāṣācandrikā, 2) Prasannarāghavavyākhyā: Timmabhūpālīyā, 3) Gītagovindavyākhyā: Srutirañjanī, and 4) Anargharāghavavyākhyā: Iṣṭārthakalpavallī. Rāmānanda mentions these biographical details in the colophon of the Anargharāghavavyākhyā. (See Krishnamacharya, V. ‘Śāstradīpikāvyākhyā: Prabhāmaṇḍala’. In The Adyar Library Bulletin, Vol. 10, pp. 63–68, 1946: p. 65)

V. Krishnamacharya gives the date that Rāmānanda copied the Siddhāntasiddhāñjana as 16th Jan 1670 AD (the 5th day of the bright fortnight in the Makara month of the year Saumya). (See Krishnamacharya, V. ‘Śāstradīpikāvyākhyā: Prabhāmaṇḍala’. In The Adyar Library Bulletin, Vol. 10, pp. 63–68, 1946: p. 67).

For the name Rāmabhadra Bhagavatpāda, see Raghavan, Venkataraman. Śāhendravilāsa of Śrīdhara Veṅkaṭeśa (A Poem on the Life of King Śāhaji of Tanjore, 1684-1710). Tiruchi: The Kalyan Press, 1952: p. 33.
